findings.claim: The new sweep does not grade "a ceiling" — it grades any duration in a gate command's trailing comment, so a true measured-runtime or p95 note reds the offline gate and accuses the doc of publishing a ceiling nothing enforces.
findings.evidence: src/browser/eval_adapter.py:3735 `_CEILING_LITERAL = re.compile(r"(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*(?:s|secs?|seconds)\b")` applied to the whole `#` comment of any `--suite fast|invariant` line. Live against the real grader with a scratch doc containing `python3 -m evals.run --suite fast   # ~71s on an M-series laptop` -> passed=False, {'publishes_a_ceiling_nothing_enforces': '--suite fast ... 71s', 'committed': 90}. Same for `# p95 2.2s per case` -> row '... 2.2s', committed 90. Both statements are TRUE; the gate blocks the commit and the message says the opposite. The provenance claims it was exercised in all four directions (re-introduced literal, struck span, spelled-out `90 seconds`) — none of the four is a non-ceiling duration.
findings.repro: write `docs/_scratch.md` = "```bash\npython3 -m evals.run --suite fast   # ~71s on an M-series laptop\n```" then run `run_case` on docs-numbers-are-derived -> passed False.
findings.acceptance: Either the literal is anchored to a ceiling word (`<=`, `ceiling`, `budget`, `wall clock`) so a timing note is green, or the over-fire is named in the case's own triage/expect.note as a deliberate cost — with one case pinning the chosen behaviour.

findings.claim: ADR-002 does not now state the truth: the Status paragraph three lines above the Ruling this PR edited still publishes 60s local / 80s CI as the enforced pair, in the present tense, via an override variable that no longer exists.
findings.evidence: specs/decisions/ADR-002-performance-thresholds.md:5 — "the ceiling is per-environment since ADR-013 Decision 3 — 60s locally, 80s on CI via `EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S`, both measured and both enforced" and "the local number ships unchanged at 60s". Enforced is WALL_BUDGET_S = {'fast': 90, 'invariant': 20} (evals/run.py:94) and the variable has been per-suite (EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S_FAST) since ADR-019 section 4 (evals/run.py:100-107). The PR's own record contradicts this: tasks/TODO.md:46 'Literals dropped rather than corrected in CLAUDE.md and ADR-002' and tasks/TODO.md:214-215 'ADR-002's [live publication is covered] by having had its literals removed'. They were removed from the Ruling only. The new grader cannot see it (not a --suite comment), so nothing catches it.
findings.acceptance: ADR-002:5 either drops its live pair the way the Ruling did, or is explicitly marked as the M12-era record (as the Ruling now does for Decision 4's 60s); and T-M32-16's 'ADR-002 ... by having had its literals removed' is corrected to match what is left in the file.

findings.claim: A third live, stale ceiling publication exists in specs/ today — ADR-013's Ruling says the local `fast` ceiling is 80s — falsifying the PR's logged claim that only two live non-command publications exist and both are covered.
findings.evidence: specs/decisions/ADR-013-fast-suite-wall-clock.md:10 — "60s locally at the time of writing, 80s since ADR-019, 80s on CI at the time of writing and 90s since ADR-019 section 5"; the 'at the time of writing' qualifier marks the 60s as historical and the 80s as current. ADR-019's own Ruling (ADR-019:6) now reads "local `fast` 60 -> 80 -> 90s (ADR-021)", and ADR-013:14 'Amended by' stops at ADR-019, never naming ADR-021. tasks/TODO.md:212-215 asserts 'The two live non-command publications that exist today are covered by other means ... A third document publishing a live pair would be ungraded.' published-band-matches-the-ledger reads only ADR-019 (eval_adapter.py:393), so ADR-013 is graded by nothing.
findings.acceptance: ADR-013:10 drops or defers its local number the way ADR-002's Ruling now does (or gains the ADR-021 amendment), and T-M32-16's enumeration of live non-command publications is corrected to the set that actually exists.

findings.claim: T-M32-17 asks for T-R35 to be deleted 'not re-audited' on the basis that all four clauses are satisfied, but clause (1) is not satisfied on this tree — two specs/ files still publish a local `fast` ceiling that is neither 90 nor even T-R35's own 80.
findings.evidence: tasks/TODO.md:229-233 claims clause (1) 'every ceiling statement in specs/ names 80/90/20/20' is satisfied. Counter-evidence: ADR-002:5 names '60s locally, 80s on CI ... both enforced' (fails the clause verbatim), and ADR-013:10 names '80s since ADR-019' as the live local number (passes the clause verbatim but is exactly the defect T-R35 exists to catch, now 10s stale). Clauses (2), (3) and (4) do check out. Deleting T-R35 as proposed drops the only tracked pointer at R2/R3.
findings.acceptance: T-M32-17's clause (1) is corrected in place to name ADR-002:5 and ADR-013:10 as still-open, or T-R35 is kept/retargeted rather than deleted until those two lines are fixed.

findings.claim: The published scope of the new check is wider than the code: expect.note says 'tracked markdown' while the sweep skips tasks/ and every dot-directory — 16 tracked markdown files, including the two skill files that document the gate commands — and the logged residual names only the shape gap, not this one.
findings.evidence: src/browser/eval_adapter.py:3944-3948 reuses md_files (SKIP_TOP = {'tasks'} plus the dot-part filter). Measured: 56 files scanned; tracked-but-unscanned includes .claude/agents/cold-reviewer.md, .claude/agents/eval-adversary.md, four .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md, 8 graphify files, tasks/DONE.md, tasks/TODO.md. .claude/skills/finish-task/SKILL.md:11-13 is a SECOND publication of the gate commands, so a ceiling re-typed there stays green forever. docs-numbers-are-derived.json:45 asserts 'no --suite gate command in tracked markdown publishes a wall-clock ceiling that is not the one evals/run.py commits' — and the criterion-5 clause in the SAME sentence does carve tasks/ out explicitly, so the omission reads as coverage rather than as a gap.
findings.repro: compare `git ls-files '*.md'` against the sweep's file set; see the reviewer's one-liner in the finding.
findings.acceptance: Either expect.note and the residual block say 'tracked markdown outside tasks/ and dot-directories', or the ceiling sweep runs over the full tracked-markdown set (it has no tasks/ false positive — that carve-out was needed for the criterion-5 phrase scan, not this one), with a case that would have gone red on a ceiling planted in .claude/skills/finish-task/SKILL.md.

findings.claim: _SUITE_CMD binds a comment to the FIRST --suite on the line, so two gate commands on one line both mis-name the suite in the red row and can hide a stale `fast` ceiling entirely.
findings.evidence:
eval_adapter.py:3734 r"--suite (\w+)[^
#]*#([^
]*)" — [^
#]* runs greedily past a second --suite. Live: 'python3 -m evals.run --suite invariant && python3 -m evals.run --suite fast  # wall clock <= 20s' -> passed=True (20 validated against invariant while the line publishes 20s for fast, committed 90). With 75s it reds but names the WRONG suite, sending the fixer to the wrong number.
findings.repro: python3 -c "import re;print(re.compile(r'--suite (\\w+)[^\\n#]*#([^\\n]*)').findall('python3 -m evals.run --suite invariant && python3 -m evals.run --suite fast  # wall clock <= 20s'))"
findings.acceptance: Either the match is anchored per-command (last --suite before the #, or a non-greedy body), or the two-on-a-line case is named in the residual block as out of scope.

findings.claim: The re-labelled OVER BUDGET source cannot report an override that happens to equal the committed number — precisely CI's configuration since ADR-021 — so a red CI run credits ADR-019/ADR-021 for a ceiling that came from the environment.
findings.evidence: evals/run.py:309-311 picks the env label only when `ceiling != WALL_BUDGET_S[suite]`; .github/workflows/eval.yml:31-32 exports EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S_FAST=90 and _INVARIANT=20, both equal to WALL_BUDGET_S since ADR-021 converged them. The branch condition is pre-existing; the collision it papers over is new. Related: eval_adapter.py:4168, the docstring of the grader that pins this very message, still opens 'ADR-002 Decision 4's wall-clock ceiling' — the attribution this PR corrected everywhere else.
findings.repro: EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S_FAST=90 .venv/bin/python -c "import evals.run as R;print(R.wall_budget('fast')==R.WALL_BUDGET_S['fast'])" -> True, so the env branch is unreachable on CI.
findings.acceptance: The source is decided by whether the variable is set (and positive), not by whether its value differs — or the case that pins this message asserts the CI-equal-value path explicitly.
findings.route_note: LOW and pre-existing in the branch condition; this PR only changed the string. The eval_adapter.py:4168 docstring half is a one-line attribution fix and rides with it.
